item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Personally, I love this thing. Its elegance is in its simplicity. Why is this thing anomalous and terrifying? Not because of some complex cognitohazard or a religious connotation - we have SCP-3000 for that. It's just so unbelievably, terrifyingly huge. It plays on that primal fear of something being so utterly massive. And because we don't know the full extent, just a guess in the thousands of kilometers, it still has that fear of the unknown. There is a lot in the SCPverse already as the site has grown increasingly complex, so the only way for this to really stay as interesting is to be just so absurdly big, and the inclusion of Bloop is a nice touch too. However, I do think that if we really did need to change the size somewhat, I'd say converting the 2-8000km size into area or even volume rather than just length. Maybe mention that much of it is concealed by rock formations that have grown over time. I'd consider suggesting that maybe the rocks themselves could be anomalous, but that just complicates it further. And the containment procedure, that nothing on earth could ever possibly contain it, yeah that makes sense considering that it's that big. It may be unrealistic in how large it is, but that just reiterates that the most anomalous thing about it, and the most interesting and terrifying thing about it, is that something the size of a continent or more has been lying there since Pre-Cambrian times.
TL;DR, this is getting an upvote from me.

item.content:encoded:
The size? Honestly, I don't get the problem. This leviathan slept for god knows how long and just became a part of the Earth's mass. And I mean, it might have been covered by the rocks at the bottom of the ocean, enough that we barely can't even see it. It might be a tectonic plate on its own. With that, saying 17% of the Earth's mass is actually an alive, sleeping monster is quite the scary thing. Also, I wouldn't be surprised if this SCP is an anomaly that defies gravity. We had weirder SCPs.

So, it snores and rustles a tiny bit which causes problems, but it's otherwise fine until it actually really does decide to wake up some day. Or if we nuke its face to wake it up…

Here's the REAL problem I have with this article. And it's the opener sentence, too, making this a bad first impression. "Because of its size, SCP-169 cannot and almost certainly will never be contained—no structure on Earth is large enough or strong enough to contain SCP-169."

Just… the SCPverse is so large now that SCP-169 doesn't really feel like such a big deal as it used to be. You can feel the age ooze from that single sentence alone. And even then "almost certainly will never be contained" is a weird phrase to use.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
See, the bizarre thing about lobsters is that they don't really age, in the sense that they don't get weaker or start getting arthritis in their claws as time passes. Instead, they just keep getting bigger and bigger. That's how you can wind up eating the meat of a creature that was born just after the Civil War and who, had it been captured earlier, could have realistically been eaten by Thomas Edison.

The most amazing part is that lobsters don't suffer through their old age like we do, unless you count the existential angst that probably starts kicking in after the first century. As they keep accumulating years, they don't lose function or get slower — they actually get more powerful. When they grow so big that their shells can no longer contain them, they simply shed it and grow a new one and keep on trucking.

In fact, scientists believe that lobsters only get hornier and more fertile the "older" they get. We now ask you to imagine a hypothetical 700-year lobster down in some undiscovered depth of the world, meeting another colossus the same age … and boning.

Wait, is this thing a LOBSTER? :O Oh, god I gotta make a lobster SCP now T_T

item.content:encoded:
I'm sorry, but I just can't get over the idiotic size of this thing and the fact that we're not allowed to fix it after EIGHT YEARS of people pointing out how dumb it is. A living creature the size of a CONTINENT? DRIFTING AROUND? And no one but the Foundation and NASA has ever noticed? Give me a break.

There are so many better ways to do this. Just off the top of my head:

1. Make it smaller. 1000 km is at least slightly plausible and still plenty big enough to wreak havoc if it ever woke up.

2. Or…have it stationary and partially embedded in the sea floor. Its back could still stick up and be something more than a few islands no one's ever heard of. If you're going to go big, go BIG. What if the Antarctic ice sheets formed over its shell and New Zealand is its tail spikes?

3. Or how about all we can see of it is the (extremely large but not SO ridiculous) head and maybe a forelimb, because the rest is (presumably) buried in the deep layers of the Earth?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Nice to see a Bloop SCP. I was thinking of doing one, figured "too late" so I checked and here it is :)

Do keep in mind though the information given about the case. that the sound was recorded 5,000 km away. You're creature is bigger than it's own call :p or just slightly under. I did a little research on the Bloop and calculated length to be 450km in total. Small enough to hide in Point Nemo. Not to mention living. How does a creature like that eat? He'd have to eat entire pods of whales for an appetizer. At 450km, with a call of 5,000 km, it's still a sizeable keter class that could feed itself by drawing prey to it? There has to be a known, or at least a theorized way that something so big could keep itself alive?

Just remember, the original "bloop" creature is supposed to 15X bigger (roughly) than a blue whale, which can measure in at 30km. Yours is……. (creepy) 66.6 times larger than a blue whale. I'd say the highest believable size, compared to the data on the real world event, would be 20X larger, which would be about 600km. I'd say the best part of making an SCP like this is making it seem as real as possible. That way, if someone found your document while looking for the bloop, it would look like a believable file and REALLY creep them out for a few minutes!

Edit: Re-read it, and I'm actually enjoying the correlations. Is it both Archipelago and Dougherty Island? I'm getting a strong hint it is.

item.title: Edit
item.content:encoded:
I'd like to formally request permission to edit this article.

This section makes no sense:

Dr. ████████ and Dr. ██████████ [Ɣ6-0421] estimate SCP-169's body length to be between 2000 and 8000 km. The creature is >thought to have existed since the pre-Cambrian era. No other specimens have been sighted. Almost nothing is known about SCP-169's >habits, such as its reproductive capabilities (if any), food source, and nesting area (if any). Research regarding SCP-169 is pending >approval.

You can't just say something is Precambrian. You would need to establish the age of the oldest strata on the islands that rest on the organism's back. Furthermore the suggestion that it is Precambrian comes out of nowhere from a paleontological standpoint because the earliest known arthropods are from the Cambrian.
